title: Model Predictive Control for a Multiport 4L NPC DAB Converter Under Unbalanced and No-Load Conditions
abstract: Multilevel (ML) neutral-point-clamped (NPC) dual-active-bridge (DAB) topologies have emerged as a promising solution for multiport dc-dc power conversion systems. In particular, the 4L NPC DAB is a promising solution for the auxiliary power module (APM) in electric vehicles (EVs) featuring a multiple-voltage architecture in their auxiliary system (AS). By connecting three low-voltage (LV) battery modules between the 4L dc-link nodes, multiple dc ports with different operating voltages are obtained. Then, EV auxiliary loads can be grouped according to their optimum voltage ratings and supplied from three distinct-voltage dc ports. In this configuration, the main challenge is to regulate the state of charge (SoC) of the LV-battery modules. For this purpose, this paper proposes a moving-discretized-control-set model predictive control (MDCS-MPC) for a 2L–4L NPC DAB in the EV APM application. The proposed control strategy combines the adjustment of modulation angles with the use of redundant switching patterns to regulate the LV-battery modules SoC in a wide operating range, including no-load conditions in the partial-voltage dc ports. Hardware-in-the-loop experiments verify the real-time performance of the proposed control.
title_zh: Model Predictive Control for a Multiport 4L NPC DAB Converter Under Unbalanced and No-Load Conditions

title: An Integrated Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Cell-to-Pack Imbalance Prediction in Electric Vehicle Battery Systems
abstract: This study presents a machine learning framework for predicting cell-to-pack imbalance in electric vehicle batteries. A set of battery attributes that affect battery performance, including State of Charge (SOC), State of Health (SOH), temperature (including ambient temperature and humidity), and cabin temperature, were used to make this prediction. The collected battery data were pre-processed to improve prediction performance. Three preprocessing methods were used: (i) Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD); (ii) deep denoising autoencoders, and (iii) feature selection using minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance (mRMR) mutual information. This preprocessing step removes noise from the dataset and identifies useful information for prediction. Cell-to-pack imbalance prediction was performed using three interpretable machine learning models: (i) an Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM); (ii) fuzzy regression; and (iii) RuleFit. These models provide transparent predictions and help in understanding the factors responsible for battery imbalance. Models were evaluated on an independent 20-sample test set held out from the 100-record dataset. Among the three interpretable models, Fuzzy Regression achieved the strongest predictive performance (R² = 0.998), followed by RuleFit (R² = 0.976), while EBM achieved a lower R² of 0.201 on this independent test set despite providing detailed feature-level explanations. These results indicate that combining signal preprocessing, feature selection, and interpretable regression can provide useful and explainable information for cell-to-pack imbalance prediction, while also showing that performance can vary substantially between interpretable models on a small, two-pack dataset; validation on larger and more varied battery datasets is needed to confirm generalizability.
venue: International Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
title_zh: An Integrated Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Cell-to-Pack Imbalance Prediction in Electric Vehicle Battery Systems

title: Centralized vehicle-to-grid coordination for behind-the-meter value in commercial fleets: Evidence and deployment lessons from a pilot demonstration
abstract: Vehicle-to-grid operation in commercial fleets remains debated due to interoperability limits, user acceptance, warranty concerns, and regulatory uncertainty. This paper reports a five-week multi-site pilot demonstration in mainland Portugal evaluating a centralized coordination architecture that uses V2G and low-complexity rule-based control to capture behind-the-meter value: energy arbitrage under time-of-use tariffs, peak-load shaving, and photovoltaic surplus self-consumption, relying only on site telemetry, charging-session data, and conservative state-of-charge (SoC) limits agreed with fleet users. Across three sites, 374 kWh of charging was shifted from peak to off-peak periods, 150 kWh was discharged during peak periods, and 16.6 kWh of additional charging was enabled from solar surplus. These actions resulted in €20 of EV charging cost savings (a 26% cost-weighted reduction against the rebased baseline), €7.9 of site-level energy savings, and an estimated €39.4 reduction in demand-related charges, modest and highly site-specific values. Average departure SoC decreased from 96% to 79% but remained above the agreed 50% minimum throughout the pilot. Beyond these outcomes, the study draws deployment lessons on measurement uncertainty, control-interval limits, plug-in behavior, battery-condition observability, protocol maturity, deployment cost, and regulatory constraints.
title_zh: Centralized vehicle-to-grid coordination for behind-the-meter value in commercial fleets: Evidence and deployment lessons from a pilot demonstration

title: Recent Advances and Future Perspectives in Thermal Runaway Prevention and Control of Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Widespread deployment of lithium-ion batteries in energy storage and transportation increases the need to prevent and control thermal runaway and associated hazards. Focusing on energy storage systems using lithium iron phosphate batteries while drawing on other battery chemistries, this review examines failure mechanisms, hazard evolution, mitigation technologies, and engineering applicability. It analyzes coupled interfacial reactions, material transformations, and structural failure, alongside the effects of chemistry, state of charge, capacity, and aging. Multisignal warning and intervention, passive thermal barriers, active fire suppression and cooling, and combined strategies are compared in terms of mechanisms and operating conditions. Engineering assessment addresses experimental comparability, maturity, scalability, cost, and environmental safety. The synthesis identifies flame extinguishment, cell thermal stabilization, and propagation prevention as distinct objectives requiring complementary indicators. Warning effectiveness depends on timely intervention, whereas barrier–cooling integration depends on heat-transfer pathways, agent accessibility, and sustained supply. Technology selection therefore requires validation at the intended scale under relevant application constraints. Future priorities include linking warning to intervention, integrating barriers with sustained cooling, and developing evaluation frameworks with clearly defined applicability. Engineering validation should also incorporate long-term reliability, life-cycle costs, environmental impacts, and personnel safety to support application-specific mitigation strategies.
title_zh: Recent Advances and Future Perspectives in Thermal Runaway Prevention and Control of Lithium-Ion Batteries

title: Prediction Modeling and Optimization of Power Grid Energy Storage System Based on Machine Learning
abstract: The rise of renewable energy, like solar panels and wind turbines, stems from price hikes and emissions rules. Weather affects energy production from solar farms. The power operations like pneumatic transports. Challenges with grid capacity arise from renewables’ growth. The power market shifts from government control to deregulation. Regulations affect energy expenses, efficiency, and environmental impact benefits. To address this issue, the authors propose a technical solution that allows the EPGCCS system combines Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) with solar photovoltaic (PV), battery storage, and grid management to enhance pneumatic transport plant efficiency. It involves designing the plant, simulating processes, optimizing mathematically, developing control systems, initializing renewable energy sources, and optimizing scheduling through DRL. The plant integrates PV modules, inverters, a battery system, grid connection, and an air transport system for energy-efficient material handling. Simulation involves random arrivals and airflow calculations using the Hudson formula. The PV system uses performance mappings and cloud forecasting, while battery management employs a flexible state-of-charge estimation method. A model combining Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) and Model Predictive Control (MPC) was created to optimize costs under set constraints. Enhancements like Priority Experience Replay (PER), adaptive noise exploration, and improved Adadelta optimization methods were added to enhance convergence rate, scheduling, and computational efficiency for automated day-ahead scheduling and real-time operational efficacy.
venue: The International Journal of Maritime Engineering
title_zh: Prediction Modeling and Optimization of Power Grid Energy Storage System Based on Machine Learning

title: Aging-Aware Attention-Driven Transformer Reinforcement Learning Framework for Sustainable Hybrid Battery Energy Management in Electric Vehicles
abstract: Battery degradation is another important constraint of the hybrid electric vehicle systems, where the standard approach to energy management focuses on short-term fuel efficiency and does not consider the long-term health of the battery. In this paper, a proposal has been made on an Aging-Aware Attention-Driven Transformer Reinforcement Learning (AAT-DRL) framework of intelligent hybrid battery energy management. Transformer-based temporal feature encoding, along with actor-critic reinforcement learning architecture, is combined in the model to encode patterns that are sensitive to degradation such as temperature, current stress and depth-of-discharge. The multi-objective reward is developed with an aim to optimize the energy efficiency, thermal safety and battery life. The framework is tested at standard driving cycles (UDDS, NEDC and WLTP). In the results, it is shown that the degradation index has reduced by 38%, the SOC has become more stable and thermal fluctuations have been reduced, with a peak efficiency of 95.3%, which is a better performance than the state-of-the-art DRL methods. The solution offers a healthy, scalable and battery management system for the next generation based on the proposed approach.
venue: International Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
title_zh: Aging-Aware Attention-Driven Transformer Reinforcement Learning Framework for Sustainable Hybrid Battery Energy Management in Electric Vehicles
